title: An Invitation to Fractal Geometry: Fractal Dimensions, Self-Similarity, and Fractal Curves
author: Graduate Studies in Mathematics, Volume 247 (AMS)
purpose: AFEL formula promotion — canonical equilateral Sierpinski gasket IFS, Example 4.33 (Chapter 4, 'Iterated Function Systems and Self-Similarity'). Fills the self-similar-construction grammar family (SKILL.md taxonomy) — direct recursive polygon subdivision (the book's own Figure 4.5 shows the prefractal approximations), a genuinely different rendering technique from the chaos-game IFS already promoted (Barnsley's right-triangle Sierpinski), even though both converge to a Sierpinski-triangle attractor.

equations.note: Eq. (4.15), Example 4.33 'The Sierpinski Gasket, Viewed as a Self-Similar Set: Standard IFS'. Visually verified against page-163.png rendered from the source PDF page 164 (printed page 134). Attractor E is the equilateral triangle with vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1/2, sqrt3/2); each phi_j contracts by 1/2. Figure 4.5 on the same page shows the first three prefractal (direct subdivision) approximations.
